surya-namaskara-a.drishti: Changes with each movement: thumbs, nose, navel
surya-namaskara-a.note: Traditionally practiced five times to open every practice.

steps.m: From Samasthitih, sweep the arms overhead, palms together; gaze at the thumbs
Fold forward, hands beside the feet; gaze to the nose
Lift the head and chest, straighten the spine, fingertips on the floor
Jump or step back to Chaturanga Dandasana
Roll over the toes into Urdhva Mukha Svanasana (Up Dog)
Roll back to Adho Mukha Svanasana (Down Dog); gaze to the navel
Jump or step the feet between the hands, lift the head
Fold forward
Rise up, arms overhead; gaze at the thumbs
Lower the arms to Samasthitih

alignment: One movement per breath. Let the breath lead and the body follow.
In Chaturanga, keep the elbows hugging the ribs and the body in one line from heels to crown.
In Up Dog, press the tops of the feet down, lift the thighs and draw the shoulders back.
In Down Dog, lift the sit bones, lengthen the spine and let the heels reach toward the floor.
Keep a steady ujjayi breath and a light mula bandha throughout.
modifications: Bend the knees in the forward folds to keep the spine long.
Step back and forward instead of jumping; lower the knees in Chaturanga.
Replace Up Dog with Bhujangasana (Cobra) if the lower back is sensitive.

surya-namaskara-b.drishti: Changes with each movement: thumbs, nose, navel
surya-namaskara-b.note: Traditionally practiced three times, after Surya Namaskara A.

steps.m: Bend the knees into Utkatasana, arms overhead; gaze at the thumbs
Straighten the legs and fold forward
Lift the head, lengthen the spine
Jump back to Chaturanga Dandasana
Up Dog
Down Dog
Turn the left heel in, step the right foot forward into Virabhadrasana A, arms up
Hands down, step back to Chaturanga Dandasana
Up Dog
Down Dog
Turn the right heel in, step the left foot forward into Virabhadrasana A, arms up
Hands down, step back to Chaturanga Dandasana
Up Dog
Down Dog; gaze to the navel
Jump forward between the hands, lift the head
Fold forward
Bend the knees into Utkatasana, arms overhead
Straighten the legs, arms down to Samasthitih

alignment: In Utkatasana, sit the weight back into the heels with the knees and feet together.
In Virabhadrasana A, square the hips forward and keep the back heel grounded.
Front knee stacks over the ankle; don't let it travel past the toes.
Keep the breath even even as the movements get longer.
modifications: Step the foot forward with the help of a hand instead of in one movement.
Shorten the Warrior stance and keep the back heel lifted if needed.
Lower the knees in Chaturanga.

steps.m: Jump or step the feet hip-width apart, hands on the hips
Fold forward and hook the big toes with two fingers and the thumb
Straighten the arms, lift the chest and look up
Fold, drawing the head toward the shins
Lift the head, straighten the arms

alignment: Feet parallel and hip-width apart, weight toward the balls of the feet.
Fold from the hips, not the waist, keeping the spine long.
Engage the thighs to lift the kneecaps; elbows draw out to the sides.
Relax the neck and draw the shoulders away from the ears.
modifications: Bend the knees as much as needed to reach the toes with a long spine.
Hold the shins, or loop a strap around the feet.

steps.m: Slide the hands under the feet, palms up, toes to the wrist creases
Straighten the arms, lift the chest and look up
Fold deeply, elbows wide
Lift the head, straighten the arms
Hands to the hips; inhale rise up and return to Samasthitih

alignment: Bring the toes all the way to the wrist creases.
Shift the weight slightly forward into the hands to lengthen the hamstrings.
Keep the back of the neck long as you fold.
modifications: Bend the knees generously and place the hands only partly under the feet.
Stay in Padangusthasana if the wrists are sensitive.

steps.m: Turn to the right and step the feet about a leg-length apart, arms out at shoulder height
Turn the right foot out, reach over the right leg and hook the big toe; left arm up
Come up, arms out
Turn the feet and repeat on the left side
Come up

alignment: Front heel lines up with the arch of the back foot.
Reach out before you reach down, keeping both sides of the waist long.
Stack the top shoulder over the bottom one and open the chest.
Lift the front kneecap without locking the knee.
modifications: Rest the hand on the shin or a block instead of the toe.
Gaze down or forward if the neck is uncomfortable.

steps.m: Feet stay wide (slightly shorter than Trikonasana), arms out
Turn to the right, square the hips, twist and place the left hand outside the right foot; right arm up
Come up, arms out
Turn and twist to the left
Come up; exhale return to Samasthitih

alignment: Square the hips toward the front leg before you twist.
Rotate from the ribcage while keeping the spine long.
Press the outer edge of the back heel firmly into the floor.
modifications: Place the hand on a block or on the inside of the front foot.
Shorten the stance for better balance.

steps.m: Turn to the right and step the feet wide, arms out
Bend the right knee to 90°, right hand to the floor outside the foot, left arm over the ear
Come up, arms out
Repeat on the left side
Come up

alignment: Front knee tracks over the ankle with the thigh parallel to the floor.
Make one long line from the outer back heel to the top fingertips.
Press the knee back with the arm to open the hip.
modifications: Rest the forearm on the thigh instead of the hand on the floor.
Place the hand on a block.

steps.m: Feet stay wide, arms out
Turn right, bend the right knee, twist and place the left hand outside the right foot; right arm over the ear
Come up, arms out
Turn and twist to the left
Come up; exhale return to Samasthitih

alignment: Hook the armpit over the outside of the bent knee.
Keep the back leg straight and the back heel grounded.
Rotate the chest upward and extend through the top arm.
modifications: Lower the back knee to the mat.
Twist with hands in prayer, elbow pressing against the knee.

steps.m: Turn to the right, step the feet wide and parallel, hands on the hips
Fold, placing the palms flat between the feet
Lift the head, straighten the arms
Bend the elbows and lower the crown toward the floor
Lift the head, straighten the arms
Hands to the hips
Come up to standing

alignment: Keep the feet parallel, outer edges in line with the mat.
Shift the weight forward into the balls of the feet so the hips stack over the heels.
Elbows bend straight back, shoulders broad and away from the ears.
modifications: Bring the hands onto blocks.
Narrow the stance or keep a soft bend in the knees.

steps.m: Arms out to the sides
Hands to the waist
Lift the chest and look up
Fold forward with the hands on the waist, crown toward the floor
Lift the head, back flat
Stay with a long spine
Come up to standing

alignment: Keep the elbows drawing back and the chest open as you fold.
Lengthen the spine on the way down; don't collapse into the fold.
Weight stays in the balls of the feet.
modifications: Fold only as far as the back stays long.
Narrow the stance.

steps.m: Arms out to the sides
Interlace the fingers behind the back
Lift the chest and open the shoulders
Fold, taking the clasped hands over the head toward the floor
Lift the head, back flat
Stay with a long spine
Come up to standing

alignment: Squeeze the shoulder blades together before folding.
Keep the arms straight and let gravity draw the hands over.
Keep the neck relaxed.
modifications: Hold a strap between the hands.
Keep the hands on the lower back if the shoulders are tight.

steps.m: Hands on the waist
Fold and hook the big toes
Lift the head, straighten the arms
Fold, elbows wide, crown toward the floor
Lift the head, straighten the arms
Hands to the waist
Come up; exhale return to Samasthitih

alignment: Pull gently on the toes to lengthen the spine down.
Keep the elbows bending out to the sides.
Keep the thighs engaged and the kneecaps lifted.
modifications: Hold the ankles or shins.
Narrow the stance.

steps.m: Turn to the right, step the feet about a metre apart, hands in reverse prayer behind the back
Square the hips and fold over the right leg
Come up
Turn to the left and fold over the left leg
Come up; exhale return to Samasthitih

alignment: Square the hips to the front by drawing the front hip back.
Keep both legs straight and the back heel grounded.
Lead with the chest; the chin travels toward the shin.
Press the palms together and draw the elbows back.
modifications: Hold opposite elbows behind the back instead of reverse prayer.
Place the hands on blocks either side of the front foot and shorten the stance.

urdhva-dhanurasana.note: Practiced three times. Many teachers then add drop backs to standing.

steps.m: From Down Dog, jump through and lie on the back
Bend the knees with the feet hip-width; place the hands beside the ears, fingers toward the shoulders
Press up into the backbend
Lower down slowly; repeat three times in total
Finish with Chakrasana or by sitting up for Paschimottanasana

alignment: Keep the feet parallel and hip-width; knees track over the toes.
Press evenly through the hands, straighten the arms and move the chest toward the wall behind you.
Lengthen the tailbone toward the knees rather than squeezing the buttocks.
modifications: Practice Setu Bandha Sarvangasana (supported bridge) instead.
Press up onto the crown first and pause before straightening the arms.
Place the hands on blocks set against a wall.

salamba-sarvangasana.note: Begins the closing sequence. Halasana through Uttana Padasana follow without a break.

steps.m: Lying on the back, lift the legs and hips over the head, hands supporting the back
Straighten the body up toward vertical

alignment: Carry the weight on the shoulders, not the neck, and don't turn the head.
Walk the hands toward the shoulder blades, elbows shoulder-width.
Lift through the inner legs and keep the feet active.
modifications: Fold a blanket under the shoulders with the head off the blanket.
Practice Viparita Karani (legs up the wall) instead.
Skip inversions with neck injury, glaucoma or uncontrolled high blood pressure; many practitioners also skip them during menstruation.

steps.m: Lower the straight legs over the head, toes to the floor; interlace the hands behind the back

alignment: Keep the hips stacked over the shoulders.
Tuck the toes and keep the legs straight and active.
Roll the shoulders under and press the arms down.
modifications: Keep the hands supporting the back.
Rest the feet on a chair or blocks.

steps.m: Bend the knees down beside the ears; arms stay interlaced behind the back

alignment: Let the knees rest lightly by the ears without forcing.
Keep the neck long; breathe into the back of the ribs.
modifications: Stay in Halasana.
Keep the knees above the forehead, not touching the floor.

steps.m: Return to shoulderstand, fold the legs into Padmasana and balance the knees on the palms with straight arms

alignment: Fold the lotus without using the hands if possible; protect the knees.
Press the knees gently into the palms to lengthen the spine.
modifications: Cross the legs simply instead of lotus.
Keep the hands on the back for support.

steps.m: Draw the lotus down toward the chest and wrap the arms around the thighs

alignment: Round the back and draw the knees toward the shoulders.
Keep the weight on the upper back, not the neck.
modifications: Hug the knees in a simple cross-legged position.
Keep the hands supporting the back.

steps.m: Roll down with the legs in lotus, arch the back onto the crown of the head and hold the feet

alignment: Lift the chest high; keep most of the weight off the head.
Press the knees toward the floor.
modifications: Keep the legs straight on the floor and prop up on the forearms.
Place a block under the upper back.

steps.m: Release the lotus, extend the legs at about 45° and reach the palms together alongside the legs
Lower the legs; Chakrasana back to Chaturanga, then Up Dog and Down Dog

alignment: Keep the chest lifted and the crown resting lightly.
Legs straight and together, toes pointed.
modifications: Keep the elbows on the floor for support.
Bend the knees.

steps.m: Kneel and interlace the fingers; place the crown of the head down, cradled by the hands
Walk the feet in and lift the straight legs to vertical

alignment: Forearms press firmly into the floor; lift the shoulders away from the ears.
Most of the weight is in the forearms, not the head.
Draw the ribs in and lengthen up through the inner legs.
modifications: Practice Ardha Sirsasana (dolphin) with the feet on the floor.
Practice against a wall.
Skip with neck injury, glaucoma or uncontrolled high blood pressure.

steps.m: Lower the straight legs until they are parallel to the floor
Lift back up to vertical; exhale lower down and rest in Balasana

alignment: Keep the hips over the shoulders as the legs lower.
Press the forearms down to keep the neck free.
modifications: Lower the legs with bent knees.
Stay in Sirsasana A or skip and rest in Balasana.

steps.m: Sit in Padmasana; reach the arms behind the back and hold the big toes

alignment: Right leg folds in first, then the left.
Lift the chest and draw the shoulder blades together.
modifications: Hold the elbows behind the back.
Sit cross-legged instead of lotus.

steps.m: Holding the bind, fold forward and lower the forehead or chin toward the floor

alignment: Keep the sit bones grounded as you fold.
Breathe slowly and turn the attention inward.
modifications: Fold forward from a cross-legged seat with the hands on the floor.
Rest the forehead on a block.

steps.m: Sit up, rest the hands on the knees in Jnana Mudra

alignment: Sit tall with the crown lifting and the chin slightly down.
Relax the face; keep the breath long and even.
modifications: Sit in half lotus or cross-legged on a cushion.
Never force the knees; the rotation comes from the hips.

steps.m: Place the hands beside the hips and lift the lotus off the floor
Swing back to Chaturanga; Up Dog, Down Dog, jump forward and return to Samasthitih

alignment: Press firmly through the hands and straighten the arms.
Draw the knees up toward the chest with strong bandhas.
modifications: Lift the hips only, leaving the knees on the floor.
Place blocks under the hands.

steps.m: Lie on the back, release the breath and rest completely

alignment: Let the breath return to normal and soften the whole body.
Keep the body warm and still.
modifications: Place a bolster under the knees.
Rest on the side if lying flat is uncomfortable.
